purpose: Restore the previously compressed Branch-B land-vehicle layer. Japanese tanks, tankettes, armored cars, prime movers, trucks, recovery assets and engineer vehicles remain recognizable historical families and quantities unless a dated ledger says otherwise, but their production median, running gear, serviceability and short-window reappearance are not identical to historical Japan.
authority_note: TECH_INDEX_v009 remains authority. This vehicle overlay implements the already-carried mandatory GALVANIC factor and the legacy '怖いときのチハ' causal line; it does not create a universal armor or mobility multiplier.
causal_architecture: compute/metrology -> tolerance stack and test plans
production QC -> smaller bad-lot and early-failure tail
parts cataloging and maintenance planning -> higher dispatchability and faster return-to-service
recovery/repair allocation -> repeated local appearance inside a 24-72 hour window
actual hull count + terrain + fuel + crew + enemy suppression -> event-local combat effect

platform_families.historical_identity_guard: Type 95-class armor, 37mm gun class, three-man ergonomic limits and basic silhouette remain. No Sherman parity, no stabilized fire and no unexplained radio fit.
branch_differences: track-pin, bearing, roadwheel and spring production median
fewer early mechanical dropouts and faster replacement of common running-gear faults

working_band.short_window_return_to_service_relative: +15-35% for repairable running-gear and powertrain faults
working_band.72h_effective_reappearance_cycle: 1.3-1.6x historical-equivalent only in maintained formations with maneuver room; on bombarded atolls use the lower 1.1-1.3x local band

platform_families.combat_limit: Thin armor and the 37mm class remain unable to win a centered frontal duel with M4 medium tanks. Value is mobile firepoint, flank shot, infantry-support fire and local reserve movement.

platform_families.historical_identity_guard: Type 97/Type 97 Kai-class mass, armor and gun families remain date- and unit-gated. No automatic 47mm conversion, extra tank regiment or Chi-He back-port.
branch_differences: sight mounting and bore/munition lot repeatability
maintenance intervals, component exchange and recovery planning

working_band.short_window_reappearance: up to 1.3-1.6x historical-equivalent in road-axis/mobile campaigns; terrain and recovery access dominate

platform_families.combat_limit: No armor or gun-energy multiplication. Sherman and modern Allied antitank systems retain decisive frontal-overmatch advantages.

platform_families.historical_identity_guard: Existing Type 92/94-class and unit-specific vehicles only.
platform_families.working_band: Operational availability +5-12% where roads, fuel and maintenance exist; negligible under artillery destruction or in terrain the chassis cannot traverse.
platform_families.combat_limit: Reconnaissance, convoy/security and mobile-machine-gun roles; not medium tanks.

platform_families.historical_identity_guard: No free increase in physical vehicle count or motorization establishment.
branch_differences: standardized service schedules and fault codes
better bearings, seals, electrical connections and cooling acceptance
spare demand forecasting and cannibalization discipline
platform_families.combat_limit: Does not erase Japan's low motorization, fuel shortage, poor roads or shipping limits.

platform_families.historical_identity_guard: Only traced wreckers, tractors, workshops, tools and crews are available.
platform_families.working_band: Repairable vehicle return inside 24-72h +15-35% relative when the damaged vehicle can be reached and the workshop survives.
platform_families.combat_limit: Burned, penetrated, drowned, abandoned behind the front or pulverized vehicles are not recovered by process quality.

platform_families.historical_identity_guard: No extra bulldozers, graders, pumps, generators or construction battalions without a dated allocation trace.
branch_differences: higher uptime of existing light plant
better fuel/spares issue and preventive maintenance
more reliable obstacle, revetment, runway and drainage work scheduling
platform_families.working_band: Existing-asset uptime +5-12%; physical construction output usually +3-8% before enemy suppression and material shortage.
platform_families.combat_limit: Heavy bombardment, isolation, missing aggregate/timber/cement and fuel exhaustion dominate.

maturity_by_period.effect: Type 95/97-era production and unit maintenance already show smaller failure tails and better short-operation dispatchability; formal field recovery networks remain uneven.
Wartime failure feedback and parts planning improve established units. Do not apply mature 1943 return-to-service bands to isolated or improvised formations.
Maintained tank regiments and priority island/base formations can use upper-middle dispatchability bands; shipping and theater allocation remain explicit.
The 72h reappearance concept is mature for suitable mobile formations. Bombarded atolls use the lower local band because wreck access, maneuver space and spare survival are poor.

event_application_required_inputs: named vehicle family and physical count
damage classification: destroyed, mission-killed, repairable or abandoned
anti_double_count: Do not add dispatchability after an event ledger already starts from a serviceable count that includes Branch maintenance.
Do not count the 72h reappearance band again as armor, firepower or vehicle quantity.
Do not add engineer-vehicle uptime again after fortification output already includes the same plant availability.
Do not use landing-package throughput as a second vehicle production or lethality bonus.
Do not apply mobile-formation 1.3-1.6x reappearance to a tiny atoll without recoverable vehicles, spares and maneuver space.
